connections.environment: Color and protection: a new prod connection is read-only, and every change on it asks you to type the connection name.
connections.readOnly: Glafira will not change anything in the cluster through this connection, whatever your rights are.
connections.apiUrl: The API server, as in oc login or kubeconfig: usually https://api.cluster:6443; a path is allowed (Rancher proxy). Not the web console.
connections.authMethod: Browser — OpenShift OAuth, like oc login --web. Token — oc whoami -t or a service account token. Certificate — PEM. Exec plugin — a command from kubeconfig.
connections.token: Saved in the system secret store, not in a file. Tokens from OpenShift OAuth usually expire after 24 hours.
connections.clientCert: Certificate and key in PEM format. The key is saved in the system secret store.
connections.exec: Only allowed commands: aws, aws-iam-authenticator, gke-gcloud-auth-plugin, kubelogin, kubectl oidc-login, oc, yc, rancher. Run without a shell; may open the browser.
connections.execLine: Exactly what Glafira will run. Values of variables and options that look like secrets are hidden. Any change to the line needs a new confirmation.
connections.ca: System store — the CAs trusted by your computer. Certificates — only the listed ones, like certificate-authority in kubeconfig.
connections.tlsServerName: Only if the certificate is issued for another name than the address host. Usually empty.
connections.proxy: System — the HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY variables. Or an explicit address like http://proxy:3128.
connections.favorites: Shown first in the tree. Separate with commas.
connections.manualNamespaces: If the cluster does not let you list projects, list the ones you work with here.
connections.test: Checks step by step: address, TLS, sign-in, platform and projects. Unsaved fields are tested too.

cluster.platform: Detected from the API groups and the version: OpenShift, or Kubernetes with its distribution (EKS, GKE, AKS, Rancher, Deckhouse, k3s, RKE2).
cluster.apiGroups: What the cluster offers beyond plain Kubernetes: Route, projects and DeploymentConfig (OpenShift), Gateway API. They decide which objects are shown.

kubeconfig.target: New connections go to this folder; connections that already exist keep their place, name, environment and color.

import.target: Where new folders and connections go. Existing ones stay where they are.
import.updateExisting: Connections that already exist get the settings from the file; your tokens, keys and their place in the tree are kept.
